The user message is a JSON packet with an instruction to audit whether a quotation is supported by page text. I need to choose exactly one category id: F, P, N, or U. Reply with a JSON object with item_id, category, and rationale (one sentence).

Let me examine the quote: "In the Google Antigravity section, the mcp_config.json example shows \"astro-docs\": { \"serverUrl\": \"https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp\" }"

Now let me find the Google Antigravity section in page_text. I see:

"Google Antigravity Section titled \"Google Antigravity\" Google Antigravity is an agentic development platform. Open ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json by following the Connecting Custom MCP Servers guide . Add the following configuration to mcp_config.json : mcp_config.json { \"mcpServers\" : { \"astro-docs\" : { \"serverUrl\" : \" https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp \" } } } Save the file and click \"Refresh\" in the \"Manage MCPs\" tab."

So the quote says the mcp_config.json example shows "astro-docs": { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp" }. The page text indeed shows that exact configuration in the Google Antigravity section. This matches faithfully - it's "astro-docs" with "serverUrl": "https://mcp.docs.astro.build/mcp". 

The quote says "mcp_config.json example shows" and indeed the page shows "mcp_config.json { ... }" with those exact keys. This is faithful.

So category F.
